sweller.title: Cognitive load
sweller.body: Working memory is small. Fill it with unconnected items and there is little room left to learn.
sweller.source: Cognitive load during problem solving. Cognitive Science.

edmondson.title: Psychological safety
edmondson.body: In a study of work teams, the ones where people felt safe to admit mistakes learned more. I see the same thing in my students.

craik.title: Depth of processing
craik.body: People remember words far better when they think about what the words mean than when they attend to how they look or sound.

roediger.title: Retrieval practice
roediger.body: Students who practised recalling what they had read remembered more a week later than students who read it again.

wood.title: Scaffolding
wood.body: Good tutoring adjusts the help to what this learner can almost do alone. The researchers called it scaffolding.
wood.cite: David Wood, Jerome Bruner & Gail Ross, 1976
wood.source: Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry.

ryan.title: Self-determination
ryan.body: People keep going when they feel three things: I chose this, I can do this, I belong here.

wall.label: Age 6
wall.heading: At six, English arrives like this.
wall.hesCap: A six-year-old who knows every row of that table, reaching for Vietnamese to find the words
wall.hesVh: The student tries to find the words, switching between English and Vietnamese: my dog is… ờ… nó… is… big?… cái đó tiếng Anh là gì ta… and the sentence never comes.

test.label: Age 9 · In speaking tests I ask one easy question
test.cap: A composite of answers I hear, not one student’s words. About eight in ten of my students tell me some version of this. That is not research; it is what I hear in my own classroom.
test.rel: So I don’t add to the bag. I take something out.

turn.label: Age 11 · Here is a rule
turn.after: Correct. Also useless to an eleven-year-old.
turn.a: a means one of many. I haven’t told you which.
turn.the: the means you already know which one I mean.
turn.picked: now it’s the dog. you made it specific.

guess.label: Age 12
guess.heading: Once the why lands, they start guessing. <open>Good.</open>
guess.resp: Drag a word into the gap, or tap one.
guess.note: We don’t re-read lists. We play them back.
guess.goed: Not quite, and a smart mistake. You used the rule for regular verbs. English just forgot to be regular here.
guess.wented: Not quite, and even smarter. You knew it was irregular, and added the rule anyway.
guess.went: Yes. And notice you had to pull it out of your head. That pull is the practice.

six.label: Age 14
six.heading: Same task. Three students. <open>Three ways in.</open>
six.pv0: Draw it badly. Then tell me everything I’d get wrong about it.
six.pv1: Write three true things and one lie. I’ll try to catch the lie.
six.who3: The one who has to win
six.pv2: Ten seconds. I’m counting your words. Go.

dist.label: Age 15
dist.heading: Two sentences that look almost the same.
dist.meanA: A finished story. It happened then, and that’s all.
dist.meanB: Still lost, right now. I can’t get in.
dist.why: have is the why: you still have the result now. The past, carried into the present.

own.label: Age 17 · Same question, eight years later
own.cap: A composite. Every part of it is something a student has said to me.

approach.label: Approach
approach.lede: I explain what a piece of language is for before asking anyone to remember it. Here are five reasons, each with the research behind it.

r1.h: Why explain the reason before the rule?
r1.lead: Because meaning is what memory holds on to.
r1.rest: When a child knows what “the” is for, the rule stops being a sentence to memorise and becomes something they can work out again on their own.

r2.rest: A wall of tables fills it before anything can be learned. Fewer items, each with a reason, leave room to think.

r3.lead: Because people learn more where it is safe to be wrong.
r3.rest: In my room a wrong answer is a clue about what the student is thinking, and nobody is embarrassed by one.
r3.cite: Edmondson, 1999 · Psychological safety (a study of work teams)

r4.h: Why play it back instead of re-reading?
r4.lead: Because recalling something strengthens it more than reading it again.
r4.rest: Games and quick challenges make students pull language out of their heads, which is the practice that sticks.

r5.lead: Because the right help depends on the student.
r5.rest: The same task reaches a quiet child, a competitive one and an artist differently, so I change the way in, not the goal.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what information is collected through this website, how it is used, and what rights you have over your personal data.

collected.title: 1. Information Collected
collected.lead: Information is collected when you send an enquiry through the chat or a note through the “For my students” page.
items: Your name (or the name you give me in the chat)
Your phone number or Zalo details, if you choose to share them

On the “For my students” page: the name you give, when you studied with me (if you say), your note, and whether I may show it on the student wall. Only notes you allow, and only your first name with them, ever appear on the site.
Basic technical data used for spam prevention and security, such as a timestamp and a Cloudflare Turnstile check result

purpose.title: 2. Purpose of Processing
purpose.text: Your data is used only to reply to your enquiry, give you information about lessons, arrange scheduling, and keep the website secure.

retention.title: 3. Data Retention
retention.text: Data is kept only as long as reasonably necessary to handle communication and service requests, or as required by law.

sharing.title: 4. Data Sharing and Services Used
sharing.lead: Your data is never sold. It is processed only by the services needed to run this site:
items: Chat enquiries are sent to me through a Telegram bot and stored in a Google Sheet that only I can open.
Student notes are sent to me through the same Telegram bot and stored in the same Google Sheet.
Cloudflare Turnstile checks that a message comes from a real person and not a bot, to prevent spam.

Google Analytics 4 measures how the site is used (pages visited, rough location by city, device type, and actions such as sending a message). It sets first-party cookies (_ga) and does not receive your name, phone number or messages. Google signals and advertising features are switched off, and the data is kept for 14 months. You can block it with the Google Analytics opt-out add-on or any content blocker.
Sentry monitors technical errors. Phone numbers and form contents are removed before anything is sent, and IP addresses are not stored.

rights.title: 5. Your Rights
rights.text: You can ask for access to, correction of, or deletion of your personal data by messaging me on <zalo>Zalo</zalo>, calling <phone>+84 353 88 5757</phone>, or using the chat on this site.

updates.title: 6. Policy Updates
updates.text: This policy may be updated from time to time. The effective date above shows the latest revision.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: These terms govern the use of this website and any lesson-related communication or services requested through it.

scope.title: 1. Scope of Services
scope.text: Services include English teaching sessions and related communication support. The final lesson format and schedule are confirmed directly with you after your enquiry.

booking.title: 2. Booking and Confirmation
booking.text: A place in a class is confirmed only after you and I have agreed directly. Availability is limited and may change without notice until it is confirmed.

client.title: 3. Client Responsibilities
items: Provide accurate information about the learner so I can place them well.
Respect the agreed schedule and communication timelines.

cancel.title: 4. Cancellations and Rescheduling
cancel.text: Cancellation and rescheduling rules are given when you book. Repeated no-shows or last-minute cancellations may mean losing a reserved place.

use.title: 5. Acceptable Use
use.text: This website may not be used for abuse, spam, scraping, or unlawful activity. I may restrict access or communication to protect my work and the safety of others.

liability.title: 6. Liability and External Services
liability.text: I make reasonable efforts to keep the information on this website accurate, but I cannot guarantee that all content is complete or free of errors at all times. Third-party services and links are governed by their own terms and policies.

contact.title: 7. Contact
contact.text: For legal or service questions, message me on <zalo>Zalo</zalo>, call <phone>+84 353 88 5757</phone>, or use the chat on this site.
